en.title: Minimum Energy to Take All Luggage From Both Ends
en.description:
Each time, take the leftmost or the rightmost remaining bag. Taking a bag of weight w from the left has base cost w·X, and from the right w·Y. If this take and the previous one are both from the left, add El; if both are from the right, add Er; the first take has no consecutive cost. Take all the bags and find the minimum total energy.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n X Y El Er and the second line contains weights. The original statement gives no value bounds; on this site 1≤n≤200000, 0≤weights[i],X,Y,El,Er≤10^9. Output the exact integer, which may exceed 64 bits.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 576, 15 and 0. In the second example, take 5 from the left and 1 from the right, avoiding the extra cost of 100 for two left takes in a row.
hints: Enumerate the final number of left takes l and right takes r=n−l. The base cost is uniquely determined by the first l items and the last r items, and the minimum numbers of consecutive left/right repeats are max(0,l−r−1) and max(0,r−l−1) respectively. Accumulate prefix sums and enumerate to find the minimum.
